skill.name: explainer-high-energy
skill.description: Create 12-20 second product promos with beat-synchronized typography, connected shape transitions, synthesized audio, and code-driven MP4 rendering.
skill.summary: Build short product promos as interactive HTML, then render review drafts and final MP4 videos with audio.
skill.author: barty-bart

security_audit.summary: All 57 static alerts are false positives for their reported patterns, including Markdown backticks, relative documentation links, audio serialization, and expected rendering operations. Two contextual renderer risks remain: recursive deletion of a predictable temporary directory and relaxed local-file access when rendering untrusted HTML. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential harvesting, or intentional data exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Contact-sheet cleanup recursively deletes an output-derived directory that may already contain unrelated files.
remediation.suggestion: Create a unique directory with mkdtemp and delete only that owned directory in a finally block. Refuse collisions with existing output files.

remediation.issue: The renderer enables cross-file access for supplied HTML without restricting browser requests.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --allow-file-access-from-files by default. Serve approved assets through an isolated local server and block other file and network requests.

semantic_findings.title: Recursive Cleanup Can Delete Existing User Files
semantic_findings.description: The stills workflow reuses out + '.frames' with recursive mkdir, then deletes that entire directory recursively. Existing unrelated contents can be deleted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: mkdirSync permits an existing directory, and rmSync recursively removes it without ownership checks. Data loss requires an existing directory at the derived path.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Render Pages Receive Expanded Local File Access
semantic_findings.description: Chromium opens the supplied HTML with --allow-file-access-from-files and no request restrictions. Untrusted page scripts could read accessible local files and transmit their contents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The launch flag explicitly relaxes file-origin access, while pages load without request filtering. Exploitation requires untrusted HTML; no actual exfiltration payload was found.

content.value_statement: Short product promos need clear messaging, coordinated motion, and synchronized sound. This skill guides HTML animation and MP4 rendering with beat-based scenes and synthesized audio.
actual_capabilities: Collect a product brief and plan six to eight scenes for a 12-20 second promo.
Specify beat-synchronized typography, connected shape transitions, product interactions, and HUD overlays.
Guide deterministic HTML animation with time-based frame seeking and seeded visual effects.
Schedule synthesized music and effects through Web Audio, or incorporate a supplied music track.
Provide a Playwright and ffmpeg renderer for contact sheets, draft videos, motion-blurred finals, and silent copies.
Require supplied evidence for product claims and restrict logo use to authorized assets.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later, Playwright, Chromium, and ffmpeg; these dependencies are not bundled.
Provides instructions and renderer source, not a finished product animation or automatic access to private product interfaces.
High frame rates, motion blur, and parallel rendering can consume substantial processing time and memory.
The included renderer needs temporary-directory and local-file access hardening before use with untrusted inputs.

use_cases.title: Product Launch Teaser
use_cases.description: Turn an approved product brief into a short launch video with a clear message, branded typography, and an end card.

use_cases.title: Vertical Campaign Promo
use_cases.description: Plan a portrait-format promo using verified benefits, supplied brand assets, and synchronized music.

use_cases.title: Code-Based Motion Prototype
use_cases.description: Develop a seekable HTML animation, inspect scene contact sheets, and review a draft before rendering the final video.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Create a First Promo
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 15-second promo for [product], which [verified function]. Use the default landscape format and synthesized music. Ask for missing brief details together.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a product name and a short factual description.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Apply Brand Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a 9:16 promo for [product] using [brand colors] and [supplied fonts]. Emphasize [verified benefit]. Use only these approved claims: [claims].
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a branded portrait video with controlled messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Synchronize a Supplied Track
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 12-20 second promo using [approved music file]. Match scene changes to its measured tempo. Include [real interaction] and [approved call to action].
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate product animation with an existing soundtrack.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Review and Render Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Build deterministic HTML from [approved beat sheet]. Use unique temporary directories and restricted browser access. Review contact sheets and a draft before final rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: Manage a reviewed rendering workflow with explicit security safeguards.

output_examples.input: Create a 15-second landscape promo for a task app. Approved message: group tasks by project. No statistics or website provided.
output: Opening: an accent line expands into the product name.
Message: kinetic words introduce project-based task organization.
Product moment: a task moves into a named project.
Closing: the product name returns without unsupported statistics or offers.
Review package: a scene beat sheet, interactive HTML preview, and draft MP4.

output_examples.input: Prepare a portrait promo for a supplied brand, using its approved tagline and music file. Provide a review stage before final export.
output: Format: 1080 by 1920 with six connected scenes.
Timing: scene transitions follow the supplied track's measured tempo.
Review: contact sheets identify typography, framing, and transition issues before draft approval.
Final deliverables: interactive HTML, an MP4 with audio, and a silent MP4.

best_practices: Provide verified product wording, authorized brand assets, and one main message before planning scenes.
Review contact sheets and the draft for readability, accurate claims, and synchronization before starting the final render.
Render trusted HTML in an isolated workspace after hardening temporary-directory cleanup and browser file access.
anti_patterns: Inventing customer counts, ratings, discounts, or testimonials to make the promo appear more persuasive.
Adding too many ideas per scene or using text that cannot be read during its display time.
Rendering untrusted HTML with expanded file access or reusing an output directory containing unrelated files.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Rendering also requires a local environment with the stated dependencies.

faq.question: What files does the workflow produce?
faq.answer: The workflow produces interactive HTML, review stills, a draft MP4, and final video exports. Audio export requires the page's audio-building function.

faq.question: Which video lengths and formats are covered?
faq.answer: The style targets 12-20 seconds, with a 15-second default. Standard formats are 1920 by 1080 and 1080 by 1920.

faq.question: Can it use my brand and website?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use supplied colors, fonts, and authorized logos. A supplied website provides product wording and brand references.

faq.question: Does it require a music subscription?
faq.answer: No. The instructions describe synthesizing music and effects with Web Audio. You can instead supply a music file you are authorized to use.

faq.question: Is the included renderer suitable for untrusted HTML?
faq.answer: Not without hardening. Restrict browser file access and requests, and replace predictable recursive temporary-directory cleanup before rendering untrusted content.
